correctness.rationale: The pinned source defines the exact Frucht edge list and an explicit LCF relabeling. A fresh independent finite reconstruction enumerated its full 168 independent simplices (face vector (12,48,73,34,1)) and rebuilt every staged Morse matching on the complete graph plus twelve deletions and twelve closed-neighborhood links. Every directed Hasse diagram was checked acyclic, yielding one critical 0-cell and ranks 3,2/3/4,1/2/0 in exactly the stated cases. Source also supplies and checks four elementary link collapse sequences. Discrete Morse theory yields integral wedge-of-spheres homotopy, not merely mod-p Betti guesses. The cone decomposition K=(K-v)∪(v*lk(v)) proves that contractible links preserve the deletion inclusion; unequal second Betti ranks refute the other eight cases. This is exhaustive only for 25 fixed finite complexes.

value.rationale: The Frucht graph is a canonical asymmetric cubic test object whose automorphism group gives no shortcut for twelve distinct deletion profiles. The complete topological classification identifies all deletion-preserving vertices, all rank-changing vertices and the distinct link mechanisms, resolving a motivated finite but complete graph invariant and extending beyond the known base wedge type.

final_claim: The canonical Frucht graph independence complex is a wedge of three 2-spheres and its twelve deletions/links have exact types in three specified vertex groups, with exactly four deletion inclusions homotopy equivalences.
limitations: Only this fixed labeled twelve-vertex Frucht graph and its vertex deletions/links; no general asymmetric-cubic theorem.
Acyclic matching and collapsibility checks are exhaustive for the finite complexes, not a bibliography proof.
